questions.q: What does LAG(TotalDue) OVER (ORDER BY OrderDate) return for each row?
options: The TotalDue value from the row immediately before it in the ORDER BY sequence
The TotalDue value from the row immediately after it
The average TotalDue across all rows
The TotalDue value from the current row, unchanged
questions.explain: LAG() reaches backward to a previous row relative to the current one, without needing a self-join.

questions.q: How does LEAD() differ from LAG()?
options: LEAD() reaches forward to a following row instead of backward to a previous one
LEAD() requires a self-join while LAG() does not
LEAD() can only be used with PARTITION BY
LEAD() collapses rows the way GROUP BY does
questions.explain: LEAD() is the mirror image of LAG() — same syntax, but it looks at a following row instead of a previous one.

questions.q: In LAG(TotalDue, 2), what does the 2 control?
options: The offset — how many rows back to reach, instead of the default of 1
The number of partitions to create
The default value returned when no row exists
The number of decimal places to round to
questions.explain: The second argument is the offset. It defaults to 1 (the immediately previous row); passing 2 reaches back two rows instead.

questions.q: Without a default argument, what does LAG() return for the very first row in the result set?
options: NULL, because there is no previous row to return a value from
0, automatically
The current row's own value
An error — LAG() requires a default argument
questions.explain: The first row has no previous row, so LAG() returns NULL unless a default argument was supplied.

questions.q: Before LAG() and LEAD() existed, how would you compare each row to the row before it?
options: With a self-join — joining the table to itself on a condition matching each row to the one before it
There was no way to do this in T-SQL at all
With GROUP BY on the ordering column
With a CASE expression alone
questions.explain: A self-join was the old approach — awkward and easy to get wrong. LAG()/LEAD() do the same thing in one pass with no join.
